title: Interop validation: chunked streaming + multiplexed tool-call semantics for onboarded models
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Validate that newly onboarded models (and their pinned versions) behave correctly when exposed to chunked/fragmented streaming outputs combined with concurrent/multiplexed external tool/function calls. This ticket covers compatibility tests, a canary plan for Dedicated/Private pools, edge-case fuzzing, perf thresholds, and a rollout checklist for publishing the model performance profile. Motivation: some models produce token fragments which can split JSON/toolcall boundaries; others interleave tool invocations while previous tool calls are still resolving. We must ensure our runtime preserves semantic boundaries, backpressure, and deterministic pinning behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Deterministic function-call boundaries: When a model emits a function/tool call across multiple stream chunks, the runtime must reconstruct the call payload and invoke the tool exactly once (no duplicates or partial invocations) in 100% of deterministic test runs.

A2: Backpressure safety: Under sustained load the runtime applies backpressure without dropping partial tool-call payloads; system recovers without data loss after transient queuing spikes in canary pool.

A3: Version pinning invariants: Pinned model versions produce identical tool-call sequences and chunking behavior during regression tests across hosts (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Any behavior divergence must be recorded and triaged.

A4: Perf SLOs: For short responses (<=32 tokens) with a single synchronous tool call, end-to-end latency p95 must be <=120ms in Dedicated canary and <=250ms in Private on equivalent hardware; token streaming fidelity p95 >=99% (no malformed JSON/toolcall fragments).

A5: Observability: Console must display a per-request trace showing chunk boundaries, reconstructed tool call payload, tool invocation ID, and any retry/fallback used; traces available for 7 days in the canary window.

A6: Regression gating: Publish performance profile only after automated suite completes with zero new failures for 72h in canary; any failures add a blocking tag and require triage before profile publication.
test_plan: Unit harness: add chunk-reassembly unit tests to model adapter for 8 fragmentation patterns (mid-token split, JSON string split, nested function-call boundaries).
Fuzzing: run 24h fuzzing job that injects randomized chunk boundaries and delays between chunks, assert single-call semantics and payload integrity.

Concurrency: simulate multiplexed client streams where a single client opens N=8 concurrent streams that trigger overlapping tool calls; assert no cross-stream leakage and correct per-stream tool call mapping.

Backpressure scenarios: create load-generator that raises request rate until queue growth triggers backpressure policies; validate no partial tool-call loss and graceful degradation (queue depth metrics, 429/503 signals).
Canary: deploy model pinned version to Dedicated canary pool (10% capacity) and to a Private test tenant; run a 72h smoke + perf run with synthetic prompts and real-world prompts from recent evals.
A/B regression: compare pinned version vs latest unpinned snapshot for chunking and toolcall semaphores; collect diffs and flag any behavioral changes.
Metrics/alerts: add metric stream_toolcall.reconstructed_failures and streaming.fragmentation.incidents. Create alert on >1 failure per 10k requests.
Manual review: PM and Design sign-off on example traces where chunking previously caused malformed JSON. Attach annotated traces to the ticket.
rollback_plan: If canary shows >0 reconstructor failures or perf regressions beyond thresholds, automatically rollback to previous pinned snapshot for that pool, disable model publication, and open ENG rollback incident with tags: rollback-streaming-interp. Notify PM/SEs and affected customer contacts.
notes: Edge cases to capture: models that emit multi-part function args (arrays) split across chunks; models that stream partial tool metadata followed by tool arguments in separate chunks.
Interplay with KV cache: ensure cached prefixes don't mask chunking behavior in replay tests; replay with cold and warm KV cache states.
Compatibility matrix: record behavior across quantization variants (int8 vs int4), because kernel scheduling changes can affect chunk boundaries.
Reference artifacts: design mockups for trace UI: https://drive.redwood.example/streams-trace-mock (placeholder).
